## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `761128865fe9c1886b7e849e38c1ae323f2a6fed`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-automation/references/state-machines-and-approvals.md + none
Security-touching: yes

Rules face, PR #35310 (Fixes #35068, riders #35041 and #34237). Read: the three cards with every comment (claim 6998681086, dev report 6999131416), the PR body and file list, the net diff against `main` (merge base `3fb7025c2`), the cited code at this head through `git show`, and the 51 check-runs on this head. Nothing was built or run. The diff's two other paths (`.changeset/35068-gated-action-field-lock.md`, `content/docs/ai/tools.mdx`) are prose faces: read for agreement, the lane seat's ACCEPT.

The security line above reads yes because pitfall 2 teaches write protection: the identity a write runs under, the static read-only strip, field permissions and their 403. The seat adopting this record adds the `security` label.

### ① Derived judgments

No accept set and no published surface moves: served skill text, one docs sentence, one changeset.

The dev's premises, each read in code at this head:

- A script action body writes as the system identity, so its write to a static `readonly` field is kept — right. `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts:3899-3902` (`buildActionExecutionContext` returns the caller's envelope with `isSystem: true` and the `'action'` mark). The static strip is gated on the context at `packages/objectql/src/engine-update.ts:1411` and runs at `:1494-1518`; the predicate-update path has the same gate at `:1841` and `:1909`, and the create path at `packages/objectql/src/engine-insert.ts:864` and `:938-946`. All three action dispatch paths elevate (`packages/objectql/src/engine-repo-execute-elevation.test.ts`, header, #13866).
- A `readonlyWhen`-locked field is stripped for every caller — right. `engine-update.ts:1476` sits outside any `isSystem` test; the comment at `:1459-1468` says the system context is not an exemption there. The lock's `record` is the prior row overlaid with the payload (`packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts:900-915`).
- A field permission without `editable` lets the body through and refuses a non-system write 403 — right as far as it goes. `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts:695-697` (system bypass), `:1645-1681` (the 403). It is not the whole rule: see S1.
- A declarative `operation: 'update'` action writes as the caller — right. `action-execution.ts:4870-4883` (`callData('update', …, ec)`, never the elevated context).
- A `flow` action under `runAs: 'user'` writes as the caller — right. `packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts:1278-1280` (default `user`); `packages/services/service-automation/src/runtime-identity.ts:447-459` (only `system` sets `isSystem`).
- A `state_machine` rule is judged on every identity — right. `engine-update.ts:1669` evaluates the rules with no identity test; the only skip is `packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts:4274-4276` (`seedReplay`, `skipStateMachine`), both server-set (`packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts:94-97`) and refused for every signed-in caller at the import doors (`packages/rest/src/import-prepare.ts:431-437`).

The card's Scope 2 listed `readonlyWhen` and `state_machine` among the locks; the PR drops both as the door on the strength of Scope 1. Right: the card ordered that measurement first and made the list depend on it.

Write paths walked for the `readonly: true` arm, each a non-system write and so stripped: REST and MCP `update_record` and `create_record`, a predicate update, a signed-in caller's import (`packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts:1125-1136` adds no elevation; the historical opt-out is refused), the declarative update action, a `runAs: 'user'` flow. No path a user or an agent reaches writes that field around the gated action. The field-permission arm is narrower: S1.

Riders:

- #35041, the ladder's fourth source — right. `packages/lint/src/validate-ai-tool-references.ts:157-177` (the shared universe), `:205-207` (`mcpPrompt !== false`), `:217-218` and `:237` (the file tools join per skill); the constant at `packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts:148`, the same file as the registry and the family prefixes.
- #34237, `mcpPrompt` and the stdio exception — right. `packages/mcp/src/skill-prompts.ts:146-157` (one projection for the HTTP surface and the stdio server, `false` projects nothing); `packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts:2599-2616`; the key at `packages/spec/src/ai/skill.zod.ts:433-458` (optional; absent or `true` keeps the binding rule).

Docs page: `content/docs/ai/tools.mdx:193-195` says the same ladder (three sources in order, a fourth for a skill MCP can offer) and names `MCP_FILE_TOOL_NAMES` in `@objectstack/spec/system`, which exports it (`packages/spec/src/system/index.ts:169`, `constants/index.ts:16`). It matches.

Ratchet: `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` is not in the diff, so no row moves. `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` is 26740 bytes less its 20-byte version line: 6680 against 6801, headroom 121. `state-machines-and-approvals.md` is 23743 bytes: 5936 against 5936, headroom 0, one byte of slack. Both readings agree with the dev's.

Cuts paid for the budget, each still taught: the "Default for metadata apps" paragraph (the default path is the heading at SKILL.md:138 and ladder item 3); the ADR-0109 sentence of ladder item 1 (SKILL.md:288-295); in the automation reference the `[]` dead-end sentence (the example's own comment at `:31`, and the unlisted-`from` note at `:52-54`), ", one per field" (the bold lead of that note) and the `record.x` habit sentence (the sentence before it).

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/skills': patch` — right: served skill text only, the level every sibling skills changeset on this head uses. The docs page belongs to no published package. No `!` in the title. `Clause-②: no` — right: no schema, export or accept set moves, and nothing a consumer could author is refused or newly accepted. `Metadata-protocol: none` — right: no metadata key is touched. `Check Changeset` is success on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` is empty. The dev's deviations (model-free commit trailer, no labels sent, #35002 no longer touching the ai skill) need no ruling here.
- The dev's out-of-scope note (a `readonlyWhen` lock keyed on the target state also strips the transition into it) is right on the code read: the lock's `record` holds the incoming value (`rule-validator.ts:900-915`, `:1245-1251`). It merits a card. No lint rule names the spelling, and the data skill (`skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md:207-217`) and the docs page (`content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx:597-673`) show cross-field examples only, so an author who wants "frozen once closed" on the state field itself has no text to steer by. Proposed: p3, `domain:skills` with a lint half, verify first on a real engine, then teach `previous.FIELD` for a freeze after entry and consider an advisory lint for a `readonlyWhen` that reads its own field through `record`.
- A security item is with the seat. It is not introduced by this diff and its mechanism is not written here.
- Landing order: open draft #35002 edits `state-machines-and-approvals.md` too (+7 −11). With no headroom on that row, whichever lands second re-measures it.
- SQL push-down: no code in the diff.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no other login to name.
- Check-runs on this head: 51 completed, 34 success, 17 skipped, none red, none running. Among the green: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, every Lint job, every Type Check job, Build Docs, Check Documentation Links, Test Core, Dogfood Regression Gate.

### ④ Design judgment

`skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`

The ladder, the MCP prompts paragraph and pitfall 1's parenthesis hold against the code in ①. Pitfall 2 holds sentence by sentence against the code in ①, and its `readonly: true` arm survived every write path tried against it. Two gaps let a reader build the pattern as written and leave the transition open. No must-fix.

**S1 (should-fix) — the field-permission arm does not bind a Modify All holder, and the pitfall does not say so.**
The pitfall offers it beside `readonly: true` as a lock "a non-system write cannot set", qualified by "any set granting it wins". Field permissions union most-permissively, and a set holding `modifyAllRecords` on the object votes the edit on every field of it (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-evaluator.ts:550-590`; `packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts:1056-1071`; `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx:195-207`). A field no held set names is unrestricted (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/field-masker.ts:424-435`), so the arm also needs a declared entry. For an administrator the arm is therefore no lock: their agent, refused at the gated action, completes the transition with `update_record`, which is the trap this pitfall exists to close. The pointer target (`skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md:202-229`) names another set's `editable: true` as the winner and never Modify All. Fix in the clause: name a Modify All set as such a grant, and say that `readonly: true` is the arm that binds every non-system caller. The row has 121 tokens of headroom.

**S2 (should-fix) — the recipe moves the write to an elevated body and names no gate on who may run it.**
An action that declares no `requiredPermissions` is ungated at its doors (`action-execution.ts:1054-1066`). Its subject is loaded in the caller's read scope (`:4292-4304`), and the body then writes as the system identity (`:3899-3902`), past the object edit grant, sharing and field permissions the caller's own write answered to (`security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts:695-697`). Built as written, every caller who can read the record can make the irreversible transition through the action; REST `/actions` asks a person for no confirmation (`action-execution.ts:3087-3090`). That includes a caller the data door refused before the lock went on. The remedy is already named in this file at `:306` (`action.requiredPermissions`, ADR-0066 D4) but is not tied to the recipe. Fix: one clause saying who may run the action is stated on it, because the body does not check the caller's edit right.

N1 (nit) — both arms take every direct write off the state field, so each other transition on it also needs an elevated writer (an action body, or a `runAs: 'system'` flow; `os validate` already reds a `runAs: 'user'` `update_record` on a `readonly` field). "A field a non-system write cannot set" says it literally; a builder can still miss it. For the #34887 lane: the scenario card's other status probes (`docs/qa/scenarios/service_desk.json:849-858` expects a validation refusal on a raw status update) should be re-read against the lock before the build prompt asks for it.

N2 (nit) — "final for every writer" is true of every identity the rule judges; the two skips are server-set and held by the system principal alone (①). Accepted wording.

N3 (nit) — ladder item 4's "(same file)" means `platform-tool-names.ts`, named two items up, while the section's lead names the lint file. The constant is reachable from either; nothing breaks.

N4 (nit) — no eval pins pitfall 2 (`skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json` cases 7 and 8 cover the confirmation gate only). A follow-up eval would hold the recipe.

N5 (nit) — out of this diff, for a data-skill follow-up: the pointer target `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md:218-224` lists the exempt system writers without action bodies, and lists imports among them although a signed-in caller's import is a non-system write and is stripped.

`skills/objectstack-automation/references/state-machines-and-approvals.md`

The pointer line (`:57-58`) agrees with pitfall 2 and restates nothing. The three cuts remove restatements only (①). No finding.

S1 and S2 are open on this head and earn a delta read of their fix; the five nits are left as accepted deviations or follow-up cards.

Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CbUb7TcZK1XUAddUmQ`

**VERDICT: PASS**

Delta round. Round 1 is record 6999708959 on head `761128865fe9c1886b7e849e38c1ae323f2a6fed`: two graded findings open (S1, S2), five nits. This record reads the one commit since, `af46d3bb11` (2 files, +11/−11: `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` and the changeset), and stands on round 1 for everything that commit does not touch.

### ① Derived judgments

No accept set and no published surface moves; the delta is skill text and the changeset's matching sentence. No code, no script, no docs page and no automation file is in it.

- The S1 sentence (`SKILL.md:346-349`) — right. "`readonly: true` binds every non-system caller": the static strip is gated on the context alone (`packages/objectql/src/engine-update.ts:1411`, `:1494-1518`, `:1841`, `:1909`; `packages/objectql/src/engine-insert.ts:864`, `:938-946`). "A field permission without `editable` … binds only a caller no held set grants it, and Modify All grants it": the merge is most-permissive (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-evaluator.ts:573-575`) and the super-user vote then sets the edit per field (`:579-587`; `packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts:1056-1071`). "So an admin's agent still writes the field" follows.
- The S2 sentence (`SKILL.md:349-351`) — right. An action that declares no `requiredPermissions` is ungated (`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts:1054-1066`), the gate is asked once for every door (`packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts:520-524`), and the body writes past the caller's edit checks (`action-execution.ts:3899-3902`; `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts:695-697`). The key is the action's own (`packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts:1275-1291`, ADR-0066 D4).
- Cut A, pitfall 1's sentence on the tool-level `requiresConfirmation` (`⚠️ … was REMOVED (ADR-0033 §2; retired above)`): a restatement, no instruction lost. `SKILL.md:297-298` still says a retired `ToolSchema` key is a parse error and `:302-304` still lists `requiresConfirmation` among the retired keys, each rejection carrying its replacement. Pitfall 1 still puts the gate on the **action** (`:337-338`) and keeps "There is no `requireApprovalFor` field" (`:340`).
- Cut B, the lead's "(☁️ `ask` / `build`; …)" folded into the skills-entry sentence (`:39-41`): a restatement, no instruction lost. The edition note two paragraphs up names the `ask` / `build` agents as the cloud runtime (`:22-24`), the front matter says agents are platform-internal (`:7-9`), and the reference section carries both names and the mark (`:375-397`). The folded sentence still says agents are platform-internal and that skills are how the platform is extended.
- Evals: no `must_contain` or `must_not_contain` string of the eight cases names a phrase either cut removed. Case 1 forbids `defineAgent(` and case 5 expects the skills route: both still rest on `:39-41` and `:375-382`. Cases 7 and 8 are about `ai.requiresConfirmation` on the action, which no cut touches. No case asserts the tool-level retirement sentence.
- The `readonlyWhen` and `state_machine` sentences (`:353-357`) are byte-identical to round 1.
- Ratchet — right. `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` is 26792 bytes less its 20-byte version line: 6693 against 6801, headroom 108 (round 1: 26740 bytes, 6680). `state-machines-and-approvals.md` is unchanged at 23743 bytes, 5936 against 5936. `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` is not in the PR diff. The gate's own run (`Lint · repo & tooling gates`) is pending on this head.
- On main's new tip: neither skill file moved since the merge base, and main's #35294 edits the ratchet file on the platform row only, so both rows read 6801 and 5936 there too. None of main's 5 commits touches the code cited in either round.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and still right: `'@objectstack/skills': patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, on the PR body and the changeset. The changeset's one edited sentence says what `SKILL.md:346-351` says. Check Changeset is green on this head.

- Dev claim "S2 fixed at `:349-351`": confirmed, ① second bullet.
- Dev claim "+42 tokens, 29 paid by two same-file restatements, net 6680 to 6693": confirmed on the net (+52 bytes, +13); both cuts are same-file restatement, ① third and fourth bullets.

S1: closed

`skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` — holds. A reader of pitfall 2 now learns which lock binds every non-system caller, that the field-permission lock leaves a Modify All holder free to write the field, and that the elevated body needs its own statement of who may run it. The two ways round 1 found to reach the transition around the gate are each named beside their remedy. The two cuts remove restatement only (①). The sentences the delta did not touch were judged in round 1.
